name: EyeSpy
description: Demand-signal research tool — reads compliant sources (Reddit API, search API, Google Places reviews, RSS, open data, podcast) plus weekly manual Facebook Group screenshot capture for a region, computes a gap_score per theme and buckets them into Clear gaps/Rising but crowded/Watch, surfacing a ranked digest to feed product ideation.
location: apps/ops (/eyespy, /eyespy/[themeId], /eyespy/capture, /eyespy/sources, /eyespy/digest), this repo — live and pulling real signals from 10 sources: IOL RSS, GroundUp Q&A RSS, GroundUp News RSS, Daily Maverick RSS, CapeTalk consumer podcast, Cape Town Service Requests (ArcGIS), Google Search, Brave Search, Google Places (business reviews), plus manual Facebook Group capture. Every signal is classified demand/supply/unclear, with trend/volume counting demand only. Themes now score gap_score and bucket into Clear gap/Rising/Watch, with a Claude-written digest at /eyespy/digest (on-demand regenerate + weekly Wednesday cron). Reddit built but blocked on an account hold (see next steps). Google Trends alpha still open (low priority).

nextSteps.step: Blocked 2026-08-02: Anthropic account is out of API credits ("Your credit balance is too low") — every classification call is failing, so all new signals (including the fresh Google Places batch) are piling up unclassified. Signals themselves are still being pulled/inserted fine, nothing is lost, they just need reclassifying once credits are back
detail: Go to console.anthropic.com, click Plans & Billing, and add credits (or set up auto-reload).

Once topped up, trigger the cron a handful of times (Vercel → Cron Jobs → Run) to catch up on both the signal_type backfill and the new Places reviews — capped at 40 classifications per run, so it'll take several triggers.

nextSteps.step: Blocked 2026-08-02: Reddit is showing Albert's account "blocked by network security" on reddit.com/prefs/apps — reproduced across a different browser (Edge) and a different network (phone on mobile data), so it looks like an account-level hold rather than anything fixable on our end. Ticket filed with Reddit. Parked, not urgent — everything else (RSS, ArcGIS, Google, Brave, manual capture) is live without it. lib/ingest/reddit.ts is already built and wired in (client_credentials OAuth, r/CapeTown + r/southafrica search for "Durbanville"), just needs REDDIT_CLIENT_ID/REDDIT_CLIENT_SECRET once the account is unblocked
nextSteps.waitingOn: Reddit's account hold clearing (could be hours to a couple days) — no need to keep retrying, it won't speed it up

nextSteps.step: Parked 2026-08-02: Google Search (geo+intent) is active but returning zero signals — its Programmable Search Engine is still restricted to 4 specific sites (facebook.com, gumtree.co.za, hellopeter.com, reddit.com) since the "search the entire web" toggle never worked in Google's UI (see earlier troubleshooting). Brave Search is doing the equivalent job without that restriction (99 signals, working fine), so Albert decided not to keep chasing Google's config — left active as-is, not a bug to fix, just redundant. Revisit only if Brave ever gets throttled/removed
Provide Google Places API key
detail: Go to console.cloud.google.com, select the same project used for Search (or create one).
Go to APIs & Services > Library, search for 'Places API', click Enable.
Go to APIs & Services > Credentials, click Create Credentials > API Key, copy it.
Consider restricting the key to the Places API only under the key's settings, for safety.

nextSteps.step: Apply for Google Trends API (alpha) access — new official API (launched July 2025), free for approved testers, gives quantified search-intent data to cross-check qualitative sources. Not urgent, approval timeline unknown

Decided 2026-08-02: starting with just 2 tracked groups (Durbanville Mammas, Durbanville) rather than the original 5-10 — Albert wants to see if the weekly manual-capture workflow is actually worth doing regularly before expanding the list or committing to who runs the Wednesday session

Built 2026-08-03: the gap_score/digest layer from EYESPY.md's Processing steps 5-7. New lib/ingest/gapScore.ts computes gap_score = recency-weighted demand volume × trend multiplier × supply_ratio per theme, confidence-gated (themes under 5 demand signals can't outrank solid ones) into three buckets (Clear gap / Rising, crowded / Watch — dormant themes excluded from scoring entirely). New lib/ingest/digest.ts calls Claude (Opus) to write why_gap + a practical-fit verdict for each Clear gap theme, a differentiation note for each Rising theme, and a cross-theme rollup note when themes overlap. New /eyespy/digest page (+ 'Regenerate digest now' button, POST /api/eyespy/digest) and a Wednesday 16:00 UTC cron (GET /api/cron/digest) for the baseline weekly cadence. The live /eyespy themes table now default-sorts by bucket-then-gap_score and shows a bucket badge + supply ratio column, same buckets as the digest so both tell the same story. Migration apps/ops/prisma/migrations/20260803120000_add_digest_gap_score/migration.sql needs hand-applying via the Query tool

Generate the first real digest — click 'Regenerate digest now' on /eyespy/digest once the Anthropic credits blocker above is confirmed cleared and the classification backlog has caught up (check /eyespy/sources' Unclassified column is at or near zero first — a digest scored against a partial backlog would undercount whatever's still stuck)
